subject: Discovery recap + open-model comparison checklist for LuminaPay
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Clara Taylor <clara.taylor@luminapay.com>, Mike Huang <mike.h@luminapay.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap and proposed checklist for model comparison

Hi Clara / Mike —

Great conversation today. Quick recap + suggested next steps so we have shared alignment before Diego starts the benchmark run: 

1) Goals we heard
- Payment routing assistance & customer support triage: primary metrics are intent accuracy and slot extraction for payment fields (amount, merchant id, confirmation code).
- Latency ceiling: p95 under 350ms in your EU region for 95% of interactive flows.
- Cost sensitivity: target model run-cost <= 0.6x your current in-house cost.

2) Immediate asks from Redwood for a fair open-model vs baseline comparison
- Canonical prompt set (we'll use your 300 canonical prompts + 50 edge-case prompts) — thanks for agreeing to share these.
- Baseline snapshot: a short evaluation dump from PayGen v2 (top-1 output + ground truth) — this will let us measure regression vs improvements.
- Production-like payload profile (avg tokens in/out, concurrency pattern).

3) Our proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- Intent accuracy >= 95% on canonical prompt set OR delta <= 2% worse than PayGen v2 for critical intents.
- Slot extraction F1 within 1.5% of baseline for payment fields.
- Safety/regression: no new critical safety failures (e.g., exposing PII, incorrect payment instructions) in >0.5% of prompts.
- Latency p95 under 350ms; cost per 1k tokens should not exceed 0.6x baseline.

4) Model candidates we recommend Redwood test first (open models + quantized variants):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (8-bit quant) — fast tradeoff for short-turn interactions.
- Llama3-Chat-13B (int8) — better contextual coherence for multi-step dialogs.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (8bit, trimmed) — higher quality baseline for heavier flows if latency allows.

5) Next steps / timeline
- Mike: share the prompt set + 48hr export of PayGen v2 evaluation (confirm by Wed).
- Diego: will run the first bench run (Mistral / Llama3 int8) and return a short report + logs (CSV) in ~5 business days.
- Kimberly / Marissa: prepare a simple A/B plan for a 5% canary once we have a candidate model that meets acceptance.

Attachments: openmodel-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (draft), prompt_set_v1.txt (placeholder).

Thanks again — I’ll follow up after Diego’s initial run with concrete numbers and a proposed rollout cadence.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com


From: Clara Taylor <clara.taylor@luminapay.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mike Huang <mike.h@luminapay.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap and proposed checklist for model comparison

Thanks, Kimberly — this is great and captures everything. A few clarifications and an initial data drop: 

- I attached a smaller subset (300 canonical + 50 edge) as prompt_set_v1.txt — it’s pseudonymized but preserves slot positions and expected outputs.
- PayGen v2 export (top-1 + ground truth) will take a bit longer; Mike is on that. Expect CSV by EOD Wed.
- For latency: most of our users are on east US; the EU p95 target was aspirational — let's set p95 < 350ms global, with the understanding you may measure in east US as primary.

On acceptance criteria: we’re comfortable with a small delta vs PayGen for non-critical intents but want critical payment authorization/confirmation to be effectively parity. The safety threshold sounds right.

Also: we ran a quick internal check on Falcon-40B — cost looks high for live traffic. Would be good to see an int8 Llama3 candidate for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.txt (the prompt set was pasted into the attached file).

-Clara
Director of Product, LuminaPay
clara.taylor@luminapay.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Clara Taylor <clara.taylor@luminapay.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mike Huang <mike.h@luminapay.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap and proposed checklist for model comparison

Hi team — quick technical notes after a light pre-check of the prompt set (I ran 50 prompts locally against Mistral-Instruct-7B and Llama3-Chat-13B int8):

Summary (pre-run observations)
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (8-bit) -> very fast (<120ms median, p95 ~260ms on a single A100-like instance with our optimized kernel). Intent accuracy approx 92% on the small sample; slot F1 ~94%.
- Llama3-Chat-13B (int8) -> higher intent accuracy (~96% on sample), slot F1 ~96%, p95 ~360ms (close to your target).

Notes on measurement and comparability
- To compare to PayGen v2 fairly we need: identical prompt formatting, deterministic sampling (top-p/top-k fixed) and the same post-processing for slot extraction. Please confirm that the prompt_set_v1.txt already includes the exact pre/post-processing expectations.
- I recommend we run the full 350-prompt suite on each candidate with 3 replicates, collect top-1 responses, store CUDA kernel logs + latency traces, and compute per-intent confusion matrices.

Risks and regression checks
- Observed occasional hallucination for merchant normalization on the Llama3 sample (2/50). We'll include a targeted prompt augmentation set to stress this.
- Safety: none surfaced in 50-run smoke test, but full-run safety eval is mandatory.

Deliverables and schedule
- I'll run the full bench (Mistral 7B int8, Llama3-13B int8) and upload logs (luminapay-benchmark-logs.csv) + MLPerf-like summary to the Drive link in ~4 business days.
- I’ll also include the exact prompt-to-postprocessing script we used so you can reproduce locally.

Attachment references: I’ll upload luminapay-benchmark-logs.csv and a short README to the Drive folder.

- Diego
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
~diego_fernandez@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Clara Taylor <clara.taylor@luminapay.com>, Mike Huang <mike.h@luminapay.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap and proposed checklist for model comparison

Thanks Diego and Clara — that timeline works. A couple final coordination items so we don’t have to chase later: 

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Mike (LuminaPay): share PayGen v2 CSV export (top-1 + ground truth) by EOD Wed 18 Feb.
- Diego (Redwood): run full bench and upload luminapay-benchmark-logs.csv + short summary to Drive by Tue 24 Feb (4 business days).
- Kimberly / Marissa (Redwood): draft a 5% canary rollout plan and rollback criteria by Fri 20 Feb.
- Clara: confirm whether PII redaction is required for the exported PayGen v2 CSV or whether the pseudonymized export is acceptable.

Acceptance gating reminders (finalized on our side):
- Intent accuracy >= 95% OR delta <= 2% vs PayGen v2 for critical intents.
- Slot extraction F1 within 1.5% of baseline for payment fields.
- No >0.5% new critical safety failures.
- Latency p95 < 350ms (global).
- Cost per 1k tokens <= 0.6x baseline.

If the first bench meets all gates we’ll propose a 5% canary for live traffic with detailed telemetry (latency, error rates, quality regressions) and automatic rollback on any gate fail. If not, we’ll iterate on prompt engineering + quantization settings and re-run.

I’ll follow up with a brief Confluence-style readout once Diego uploads the logs.

Best,
Kimberly
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
